purpose: Adds an optional, default-off post-render pass (prioritizeLCPImages) that strips loading="lazy" from the first N images and stamps fetchpriority="high" on the detected LCP in the finalized page HTML, using the WP 6.9+ template-enhancement output-buffer filter with a legacy ob_start fallback for older WordPress.
riskRationale: The commit ships ~4,737 dev/test vendor files (~525K lines: phpunit, squizlabs/phpcs, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, mockery, hamcrest, nikic/php-parser, etc.) inside the production plugin, violating the repo's composer-release workflow (AGENTS.md), and .distignore only partially excludes them; the PR's file list omits them. Separately, on WP < 6.9 the legacy LCP buffer runs outside the static-cache buffer, so the enhancement is never persisted into cached HTML and cached pages — the plugin's primary traffic — never receive it, and the new PHP tests neither run in this repo (PHPUnit filename-suffix mismatch) nor exercise the HTML transformation logic.
breakingChanges: vendor/ now contains the full require-dev tree (~4,737 files / ~525K lines) instead of production-only dependencies, violating the documented `composer release` workflow and bloating the repo and the WordPress.org release ZIP
On WP < 6.9 with the static HTML cache enabled, the loading="lazy"/fetchpriority rewrites are never written into cached HTML files, so cached visitors receive no benefit from the feature

text: The feature is well-engineered in substance: get_current_lcp_url() is a clean, behavior-preserving extraction; the version-gated WP_HTML_Processor::serialize_token() path with a get_last_error() bail-out to the WP_HTML_Tag_Processor fallback follows the documented WP 6.9 approach; fetchpriority="high" is only applied when absent (no double-application); and the setting is additive and default-off in both PHP and JS. However the change is not merge-ready: it commits the entire dev vendor tree into the production plugin, the legacy WP < 6.9 path never persists the rewrites into the static cache (a no-op for cached traffic), the WP 6.9+ full-parser loop stamps every matching while the fallback stamps only the first, and the new PHP tests are not discoverable in this repo (phpunit.xml.dist suffix mismatch -> zero tests executed) and never exercise the actual Pass A/Pass B transformation.

reasoning: Must fix before merge: (1) strip dev dependencies from vendor/ via composer release so only production packages ship, (2) reorder the legacy WP<6.9 buffer so the enhancement is baked into the static HTML cache, (3) unify the multi-stamp behavior between the 6.9+ loop and the fallback, (4) make the PHPUnit suite discoverable and add tests that actually exercise the transformation, and (5) ensure the LCP image itself is un-lazy-loaded when it falls beyond the excludeFirstImages threshold.

message: Extracting get_current_lcp_url() into a reusable private helper preserves the exact data-source priority (post meta → front-page option → strategy+URL-hash transient, mobile-first then desktop) with zero behavior change to the existing autoPreloadLCP path, and it is covered by reflection-based tests for the post-meta, front-page, and empty paths.

The WP 6.9+ serialize_token() token-streaming path is correctly gated (method_exists + version_compare + class_exists, protecting against the 6.7/6.8 protected method), checks get_last_error() before returning the rebuilt document so a parser bail can never emit partial output, and falls back to the minimal WP_HTML_Tag_Processor edit on any error or older version. fetchpriority="high" is only set when the attribute is absent, so core's wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes() decisions and the plugin's existing excludeFirstImages high-priority assignment are never double-applied.

The new setting is additive and default-off in both the PHP defaults array and the JS defaultSettings (src/components/ImageOptimization.js:42), so update_settings always submits the key, stored options never silently drop it, and the callback no-ops immediately when disabled — minimizing risk to existing installs.

WP 6.9+ integration is architecturally correct: the LCP filter at priority 30 runs after cache (10) and used-CSS (20), and stash_cache() fires on wp_finalized_template_enhancement_output_buffer so the static cache file is written with the finalized, LCP-processed output.

A new Jest suite renders ImageOptimization and asserts the Prioritize LCP Images toggle renders and toggles correctly, following the established apiRequest mocking pattern, so the settings plumbing is covered on the JS side.

The commit adds ~4,737 files / ~525K lines of dev/test dependencies to vendor/ (phpunit, squizlabs/php_codesniffer, wp-coding-standards, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, mockery, hamcrest, nikic/php-parser, sebastian, phar-io, theseer, myclabs, staabm, phpcompatibility, phpcsstandards, dealerdirect) and grows the installed package list from 6 to 43. AGENTS.md explicitly requires running `composer release` (composer install --no-dev) before pushing so vendor ships only production deps (voku/html-min, matthiasmullie/minify, woocommerce/action-scheduler), and origin/master's vendor/ had exactly those. .distignore only excludes squizlabs, wp-coding-standards, dealerdirect, phpcsstandards, bin, phpcompatibility — so phpunit, mockery, brain/monkey, patchwork, php-parser, etc. would be included in any deploy path that doesn't re-run composer (e.g. SVN from a dirty tree), and the repo itself bloats by half a million lines. The PR description lists only 12 changed files, omitting these ~4,700.
suggestion: Run `composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader --ignore-platform-reqs` (the documented `composer release`), verify vendor/ contains only production packages, and commit that result. If PHPUnit tests are meant to stay, extend .distignore to exclude the remaining dev-only vendor dirs.
suggestionCode:
composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader --ignore-platform-reqs
git rm -r --cached vendor/phpunit vendor/brain vendor/mockery vendor/antecedent vendor/squizlabs vendor/wp-coding-standards vendor/phpcompatibility vendor/phpcsstandards vendor/nikic vendor/hamcrest vendor/phar-io vendor/sebastian vendor/theseer vendor/staabm vendor/myclabs vendor/bin
git add vendor/
git commit --amend --no-edit

message: On WP < 6.9 the legacy LCP buffer is registered at template_redirect priority 5 (outermost), while the static-cache buffer runs at default priority 10 (inner, class-cache.php:364). PHP flushes inner buffers first, so the cache callback writes the cache file BEFORE prioritize_lcp_in_buffer() runs — the cached HTML never contains the fetchpriority="high"/un-lazy-load changes. Because cached pages are served by the advanced-cache.php drop-in (WordPress is skipped entirely on cache hits), the enhancement is effectively a no-op for the majority of traffic on WP < 6.9; only the 6.9+ path is correct (stash_cache saves after all filter priorities).
suggestion: Start the legacy LCP buffer AFTER the cache buffer (e.g. template_redirect priority 20) so prioritize_lcp_in_buffer() runs first on the raw buffer and Cache::start_output_buffer() then stores the enhanced HTML — mirroring the 6.9+ flow. Update the docblock accordingly and verify the result is persisted in the cache file and survives a cache hit.

message: The WP 6.9+ full-parser loop stamps fetchpriority="high" on EVERY that matches the LCP URL (no break), while the fallback WP_HTML_Tag_Processor path (line 1843) breaks after the first match. When the same URL appears in multiple tags (header logo + featured image, or the hero repeated in content), all get fetchpriority="high" on WP 6.9+ but only the first on older versions — producing version-dependent HTML and diluting the browser's LCP priority across duplicate high-priority requests, contrary to the stated 'the detected LCP ' intent. You cannot simply break out of the token loop (that would truncate the serialized document), so a flag is needed.
suggestion: Add a $stamped flag so the attribute is set at most once while continuing to serialize all remaining tokens, unifying behavior with the fallback path.

message: The new PHP tests never exercise the PR's core logic. In the bare PHPUnit environment WordPress core is not loaded, so class_exists('WP_HTML_Tag_Processor') is always false: test_prioritize_lcp_in_buffer_graceful_without_html_api() only passes through the guard-clause exit, and unlazyload_first_images()/prioritize_lcp_image() are never run against real HTML. Worse, phpunit.xml.dist declares no testsuite suffix, so PHPUnit's default *Test.php filename convention does not match these class-*-test.php files and `composer test` reports zero tests executed — the claimed PHP verification cannot actually run in this repo, and no CI workflow runs phpunit either.
suggestion: Add a suffix attribute to the phpunit testsuite so the files are discovered, and add transformation tests that stub/provide WP_HTML_Tag_Processor (or run under a WP test harness) asserting: loading="lazy" is removed from the first N images, fetchpriority="high" is added only to the image matching the LCP URL, and an existing fetchpriority is preserved. Wire `composer test` into CI if these are intended to be the project's PHP test suite.

message: Pass B only sets fetchpriority="high" on the LCP image; it never removes loading="lazy". When lazyLoadImages is enabled and the LCP image falls beyond the excludeFirstImages N threshold, add_delay_load_img() will already have stamped it loading="lazy" (and possibly data-src JS-lazy), so the browser defers it regardless of the priority hint and the optimization is ineffective for the exact case the feature targets.
suggestion: In Pass B, also remove loading="lazy" from the matched LCP image (guarding on the existing-fetchpriority check) so an in-viewport LCP image is actually fetched eagerly at high priority; keep the one-shot stamping semantics.

message: tag_matches_lcp_url() uses a raw substring match (false !== strpos($value, $lcp_url)) with no URL normalization. The stored LCP URL comes from the PageSpeed API as an absolute URL, so a DOM src/srcset that is relative or protocol-relative (/wp-content/uploads/hero.jpg) or that differs in scheme/host (CDN rewrites) or size suffix (-1024x1024.jpg) will never match and the LCP image silently won't be prioritized; conversely, a prefix match can false-positive on derived assets (LCP .../hero.jpg matching .../hero.jpg-150x150.webp or .../hero.jpg2.png).
suggestion: Normalize both sides before comparing — resolve relative/srcset URLs against home_url(), strip query strings and size suffixes (-NNNxNNN, -scaled, -eNNN), and compare via wp_parse_url path/host equality — so absolute-vs-relative matches work and false positives are avoided.

message: unlazyload_first_images() counts images that have a src OR data-src (line 1783), while add_delay_load_img() (line 1940) counts only tags with a non-null src. On buffers where images carry only data-src (third-party markup, or JS-lazy placeholders), the two counters diverge, so the 'first N' set Pass A un-lazys does not strictly match the excludeFirstImages set the docblock claims to mirror.
suggestion: Align the counting predicate with add_delay_load_img() (count only src-bearing images, skipping data-src-only placeholders), or extract a shared image-counting helper used by both functions, and update the docblock.

message: With the toggle on, every front-end request pays avoidable hot-path cost: up to 2-3 full HTML parses/re-serializations per render (Tag_Processor Pass A, HTML_Processor Pass B, plus a possible Tag_Processor fallback) even when the stored LCP image is absent from the DOM, get_current_lcp_url() re-resolves post meta/option/transient on every render, and the legacy buffer is opened for feeds, robots.txt, and other non-HTML template_redirect requests.
suggestion: Track a $changed flag in both passes and return the original $buffer when nothing was modified; skip Pass B when get_current_lcp_url() is empty (already done); short-circuit when the buffer contains no '<img' tag; and early-exit start_lcp_priority_buffer() for non-HTML contexts (is_feed, is_robots, wp_doing_ajax, REST_REQUEST).

message: get_current_lcp_url() declares a ': string' return type but returns $meta_lcp / $front_lcp / $transient directly. get_post_meta()/get_option()/get_transient() return mixed; if any plugin-owned key ever holds a non-string value (e.g. a serialized array), the function throws a TypeError mid-buffer-processing on the front end. The original code tolerated mixed values.
suggestion: Cast the resolved value before returning (is_string check) or drop the strict return type.

message: The WP 6.9+ filter registration (priority 30) lacks the should_optimise_for_logged_in() guard that the legacy start_lcp_priority_buffer() applies, so on WP 6.9+ the buffer is processed for logged-in users even on sites configured not to optimize/cache logged-in views. Impact is only wasted CPU, but the two paths behave differently for the same user.
suggestion: Gate the wp_template_enhancement_output_buffer registration on the same should_optimise_for_logged_in() check used by the legacy path.
